findings.evidence: Average.lean:116 `circleAverageTransverse_eq_zero_of_odd`; Average.lean:144-157 `azimuthalAverage`, `azimuthalAverage_of_neg`, `azimuthalAverage_of_nonneg`. No `azimuthalAverage_*_of_odd` in the file.
findings.fix: Export `azimuthalAverage_eq_zero_of_odd (f : VectorTmd Flavor) (i : Flavor) {x kT Q2 ζ : ℝ} (hf : ∀ w, ‖w‖ = |kT| → f i x (-w) Q2 ζ = -f i x w Q2 ζ) : azimuthalAverage f i x kT Q2 ζ = 0`, unconditional in `kT`, proved by `rcases lt_or_ge kT 0` from `azimuthalAverage_of_neg` and `circleAverageTransverse_eq_zero_of_odd`.
findings.issue: The odd-annihilation lemma exists only at the `circleAverageTransverse` level (line 116). The roadmap's 2.4 product is annihilation of the *azimuthal average*, and a consumer holding `f i x (-w) Q2 ζ = -f i x w Q2 ζ` on the circle must case-split on the sign of `kT` and rewrite with `azimuthalAverage_of_nonneg` before the existing lemma applies; at `kT < 0` the statement is true for a different reason (the `if` guard).

findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Integral/CircleIntegral.lean:84 `range_circleMap (c R) : range (circleMap c R) = sphere c |R|`; mathlib/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Operator/LinearIsometry.lean:946 `LinearIsometryEquiv.image_sphere`. Grep of Transverse.lean finds no `range`/`sphere` lemma.
findings.fix: Add `range_radialVector (kT : ℝ) : Set.range (radialVector kT) = Metric.sphere 0 |kT|` (and/or the `mem_sphere ↔ ∃ θ` restatement), from Mathlib's `range_circleMap` plus `LinearIsometryEquiv.image_sphere` and `map_zero`.
findings.issue: `radialVector` is exported with introduction/computation lemmas only (`_apply_zero`, `_apply_one`, `norm_radialVector`, `_zero_radius`, `_neg_radius`) and no elimination: nothing says the radial vectors exhaust the circle. A consumer holding a property in polar form `∀ θ, P (radialVector kT θ)` cannot discharge the `∀ w, ‖w‖ = |kT| → P w` hypotheses that `circleAverageTransverse_congr_sphere`, `_nonneg_of_nonneg` and `_eq_zero_of_odd` all take.

findings.fix: Export `circleAverageTransverse_def (g kT) : circleAverageTransverse g kT = Real.circleAverage (fun z => g (Complex.orthonormalBasisOneI.repr z)) 0 kT := (rfl)`, and generalise `circleAverageTransverse_zero_fun` to `circleAverageTransverse_const (c : ℝ) (kT) : circleAverageTransverse (fun _ => c) kT = c` (Mathlib's `circleAverage_const` is already what the current proof uses).
findings.issue: `circleAverageTransverse` is advertised as `Real.circleAverage` transported along `Complex.orthonormalBasisOneI.repr`, but the only exported restatement (`_eq_integral`, line 69) jumps to the fully unfolded interval integral. Reusing any Mathlib fact not hand-copied here — `Real.circleAverage_const`, `ContinuousOn.circleAverage`, `circleAverage_eq_circleAverage_zero_one`, the integrability lemmas — requires unfolding the definition rather than applying API.

findings.evidence: Average.lean:88 `@[simp] circleAverageTransverse_zero_radius` vs Average.lean:159-162 with no annotation.
findings.fix: Mark `azimuthalAverage_zero_radius` `@[simp]`; the LHS has a literal `0` radius, so it cannot loop.
findings.issue: `azimuthalAverage_zero_radius` carries no `@[simp]`, while its `circleAverageTransverse` counterpart (line 88) does. Since `azimuthalAverage` is not simp-unfolded, `simp` cannot reduce `azimuthalAverage f i x 0 Q2 ζ` at all.

summary: The exported surface is minimal and free of compatibility artefacts, but the characteristic API is incomplete: the odd-annihilation result stops at `circleAverageTransverse` and never reaches `azimuthalAverage`, `radialVector` has no elimination lemma, and `circleAverageTransverse` exports no bridge back to `Real.circleAverage`.
